newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends sharply weaker as heat turns lower.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends sharply weaker as heat turns lower.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures ended sharply weaker after NYMEX heating oil, turned round short-covering led gains, traders said.
March Brent initially tracked the heating oil bounce to new intra day highs at $21.25 a barrel, but turned tail back towards the lows as weaker NYMEX products triggered selling.
The March Brent contract last traded 64 cents a barrel down at $20.54 four cents off the days low after easing through key support around Mondays $20.55 low.
U.S. traders were quick to point out the gains on heating oil were mainly as a result of short covering and there was no new buying to offer support.

Though many were heartened by the apparent growth in distillate demand which saw a fall of 4.9 million barrels in U.S. distillate stocks last week most had expected a reversal of the gains "once the shorts are covered".
"It's too late in the season for the heating oil to keep leading the market and not early enough for the gasoline to take over," one traders said.

Gas oil futures, closing earlier, ended on a firmer note on the back of the NYMEX heating oil short-covering, but the marekt was expected to be playing catch up to the U.S. markets late losses in early trade on Thursday.
The March gas oil contract last traded $2 firmer at $184.75 a tonne. The February contract expired at noon 50 cents off at $192 with a spot delivery of 558,500 tonnes.
